2607.13901.title: High-Order Question Generation in a Multilingual Educational Context
2607.13901.paper_summary: Critical thinking is a fundamental skill that helps learners move beyond simple memorization. One way to develop this skill is through high-order questioning. However, crafting such questions remains a challenge for educators, and classroom practices tend to rely on low-order questions. Large Language Models have demonstrated strong capabilities in generating high-order questions, especially when guided by prompts based on Bloom's Taxonomy. Yet, existing research has largely centered on this framework and focused only on English. This study addresses these gaps by introducing prompts grounded in two alternative frameworks: Claim-Evidence-Reasoning and Divergent Questioning within a multilingual context using Basque, Spanish, and English. Results indicate that while both an open-source and a proprietary model rather effectively generate questions in all three languages, only about half of the answerable questions are recognized by teachers as high-order. A positive finding is that the alternative frameworks produce structurally and conceptually varied questions, suggesting they could complement each other and provide viable alternatives to Bloom's Taxonomy.
2607.13901.paper_summary_zh: 批判性思維是一項基本技能，幫助學習者超越簡單的記憶。<lb/>發展這項技能的一種方法是透過高階提問。<lb/>然而，設計這類問題對教育工作者來說仍然是一項挑戰，而課堂實踐往往依賴於低階問題。<lb/>大型語言模型在生成高階問題方面展示了強大的能力，特別是在根據布魯姆分類法的提示指導下。<lb/>然而，現有研究主要集中在這一框架上，且僅專注於英語。<lb/>本研究通過引入基於兩個替代框架的提示來填補這些空白：主張-證據-推理和多元提問，並在使用巴斯克語、西班牙語和英語的多語言背景下進行。<lb/>結果顯示，雖然開源模型和專有模型在三種語言中都能相當有效地生成問題，但只有約一半的可回答問題被教師認可為高階問題。<lb/>一個積極的發現是，這些替代框架產生了結構和概念上各異的問題，這表明它們可以相輔相成，並為布魯姆分類法提供可行的替代方案。
